targets.source_scope: I23 §6, (6.9), Proposition 6.3 and §7, Proposition 7.2. The fixed-determinant fiber and its compatible trace-free complex are explicit owned comparisons.

supporting_constructions.statement: Build the total Čech complex in sheaves of ℂ-vector spaces, with coherent underlying terms and the actual C-linear first-order differentials, then prove refinement, cover independence, cone signs, trace pairing and termwise Serre-duality compatibility. Do not apply D(QCoh) to a non-O-linear differential. Identify automorphisms, tangents and obstructions by the actual lifting cocycles, for the ramified three-term cone including all factorization relations. Extend the elementary small-extension framework to the finite-dimensional square-zero kernels needed here, proving linearity, direct sums and base-change naturality rather than reading them into SSF4.5.
supporting_constructions.statement_ja: 連接な基礎項と実際の ℂ 線形一次微分作用素をもつ複体を、ℂ ベクトル空間の層の Čech 全複体として構成し、細分・被覆独立性・錐の符号・トレース対・項別 Serre 双対との両立を証明する。O 線形でない微分を D(QCoh) の射にしない。分岐因子化の全関係を含む三項の錐について、実際の持上げコサイクルから自己同型・接空間・障害を同定する。ここで必要な有限次元平方零核への拡張、線形性、直和、基底変換を証明し、SSF4.5 の基本的小拡大だけから自動的に得たことにしない。

supporting_constructions.statement: For the bounded deformation complexes on a proper complex curve, construct analytification of each differential operator through its finite-order principal-parts presentation. Prove the principal-parts analytification comparison and compatibility with composition, so that the analytified differential still squares to zero. Apply proper coherent GAGA term by term and the convergent hypercohomology spectral sequences to obtain the algebraic–analytic hypercohomology comparison, including the actual local ramified cone. This follows the proof route of Deligne II6.6. The complex is a complex of sheaves of complex vector spaces with coherent O-module terms; its connection differential is not treated as an O-linear map in the derived category of coherent O-modules. Relative base-change claims are separate and retain the exact flatness and cohomological hypotheses of the source being used.

targets.name: smoothModuliAndDeterminantFiber
targets.title: Smoothness, dimension and the determinant fiber
targets.statement:
Use §1.4 to prove obstruction vanishing and smoothness of the stable moduli family in the admitted domain. Identify its relative tangent bundle by first hypercohomology. For unfixed determinant and a nonempty stable fiber, derive dim M_b = 2r²(g−1)+2+r(r−1)deg P. The local trace polar parts are fixed in this formula.

For the fixed-determinant export, construct the determinant moduli of line connections with those trace polar parts, locally an affine bundle of rank g over Picᵈ(C_b), and prove that its tangent complex is the regular de Rham complex O_C → Ω¹_C. Over ℂ, build a compatible trace map and scalar section using 1/r at the full deformation-complex level, including ramified relations. Prove the induced determinant map is smooth on the stated stable locus, with surjective tangent map onto a 2g-dimensional determinant tangent space. Identify the specified-determinant coarse family with the relevant fiber after its gerbe comparison. Only then deduce dim M_b^det = 2(r²−1)(g−1)+r(r−1)deg P. Prove that the trace pairing splits orthogonally into the trace-free and scalar directions and is nondegenerate on the fixed-determinant tangent space. Rank-one fixed-determinant fibers are zero-dimensional.

The fixed-determinant dimension and symplectic theorems use the deformation-functor comparison, smooth determinant map and orthogonal trace splitting constructed in 1.5. Prove these comparisons on the full stated complex before restricting to a determinant fiber. The unfixed-determinant theorem and the genus-zero dimension agreement have the scopes stated above.
hypotheses: The moduli construction of 1.3 and actual complex and trace pairing of 1.4; the admitted local models over ℂ.
Dimension assertions concern nonempty stable fibers. The fixed-determinant conclusion additionally requires the determinant-map comparison proved in this target.

JacobianChallenge C–D supplies only the coherent floor and its fixed-field geometrically integral specialization. supporting_constructions.statement: Test formal smoothness locally on affine square-zero thickenings T₀↪T with quasi-coherent ideal I. Flatness identifies the ideal of C_T0 in C_T with p*I. targets.name: closedRelativeTraceForm
targets.title: Early finite-flat unfolding and the closed symplectic form
targets.statement:
Construct the relative trace two-form on the moduli family, descend it from the universal-object cover and prove nondegeneracy using §1.4 and §1.5. Prove closedness by the following auxiliary construction here, before any limiting-system or confluence application. Over a smooth integral auxiliary base H, replace the fixed polar divisor by the finite-flat divisors of I23 §8. At a ramified point use ∏ⱼ₌₁ᵐ⁻¹(z−hʳqⱼ)(z−hʳ), with qⱼ distinct, nonzero and different from 1. Construct the moduli algebraic space of simple connections with the unfolded factorized local structures, an étale universal-object cover, the relative deformation complex and trace form. Reapply the boundedness and deformation arguments to this new family; it is not covered merely by §1.1's disjoint marked sections.

Prove smoothness over H and identify the original stable moduli, complex and form with the appropriate open part of the central fiber. On the dense open parameter set with generic separated poles, construct both quasi-isomorphisms from the diagonal deformation complex to the unfolded complex and the logarithmic parabolic complex, respecting trace forms. Prove closedness of the logarithmic trace form by the Čech cup-product/trace calculation and gauge descent and transfer it through these two comparisons. The relative sheaf of three-forms on this smooth family over an integral base is locally free, and restriction to the indicated dense open detects zero. Deduce d_relative ω=0 on the whole family, restrict to the central stable locus and descend. A later nonreduced base change uses this proved identity; density on a nonreduced base is not a substitute.

The fixed-determinant result is the pullback of this closed form to the determinant fiber, with nondegeneracy supplied only after §1.5's orthogonality comparison. No scalar Hamiltonian or classification of phase surfaces enters this construction.
hypotheses: §§1.3–1.5 in the admitted domain. Smoothness, the auxiliary simple-connection family, generic comparison maps and closedness are outputs.
For the fixed-determinant symplectic export, the determinant-fiber comparison and nondegeneracy gate in 1.5.

targets.name: strongHorizontalSplitting
targets.title: Strong integrable extensions and the actual horizontal splitting
targets.statement:
For a time tangent at a moduli point, construct a strong integrable extension of the universal connection over the corresponding dual-number deformation. On the moving total curve X let D be the sum of the marked relative Cartier divisors with coefficient one, formed on the smooth ambient family before pullback to the infinitesimal base. The allowed total-form pole filtration is Ω¹_X(log D) ⊗ O_X(P−D), relative to any fixed auxiliary base. Require integrability and preservation of the kernel lattices attached to the local filtrations, namely kernels of E → E|_{mᵢaᵢ}/Fᵢ,k with the relevant structural thickening and the additional factorized relations. Preserving flags separately on each fiber is insufficient. Prove the coordinate lemma that, in a moving polar coordinate z, the allowed forms are generated by dz/zᵐ and dε/zᵐ⁻¹; the time coefficient is regular at a logarithmic point.

Prove existence and uniqueness up to the specified isomorphism restricting to the identity on the central fiber, within this strong extension class. Glue the local lifts and descend from the universal-object cover. Construct the actual O-linear splitting h:π*TB→TM and prove dπ∘h=id. In fixed-determinant mode prove that taking determinant of the constructed extension agrees with the certified rank-one transport of §1.2, so that h is tangent to the moving determinant fiber. This is a comparison theorem, not a claim that an arbitrary determinant section is preserved. Existence of h, integrability and preservation of the trace form are not input axioms.
hypotheses: The admitted time and moduli constructions of §§1.1–1.5 and a time tangent vector. The total pole filtration and kernel-lattice relations specify the class of extensions being constructed.
For fixed determinant, §1.2 supplies the verified rank-one time transport and §1.5 supplies the determinant-fiber comparison.

targets.name: flatSymplecticIsomonodromy
targets.title: Flatness, trace-form preservation and the closed total form
targets.statement:
Compare the two-parameter strong extensions and their mixed infinitesimal term to prove h([v,w])=[h(v),h(w)]. Prove that holomorphic integral sections carry the corresponding strong integrable total connections. This bracket calculation uses the algebraic extension comparison, not a global Riemann–Hilbert theorem.

Use the actual trace cocycles and strong-extension comparison to prove that the constructed horizontal variation preserves the relative symplectic form ω. Flatness of an arbitrary splitting alone would not imply that assertion. Define Ω(v,w)=ω(v−h(dπv),w−h(dπw)), prove dΩ=0 and ker Ω=im h, and deduce preservation of ω by local horizontal transport. The generic differential-form equivalence in NonlinearConnections §0.6 can organize this final calculation, but it cannot supply trace-form preservation as an unproved premise. In a one-dimensional time chart, only after a symplectic trivialization and local exactness have been supplied, derive Ω=dq∧dp+dH∧dt in relative dimension two, and the analogous sum in higher even dimension. Scalar Hamiltonians are local primitives attached to charts.
hypotheses: The actual strong splitting of 2.1 and the relative symplectic form of 1.6, with the determinant gate where applicable. Flatness and preservation of that form are outputs.

targets.name: coherentModuliNaturality
targets.title: Naturality and coherent change of presentation
targets.statement:
For isomorphic admitted decorated time problems construct compatible isomorphisms of their stacks, rigidifications and phase families, preserving the trace pairing, ω, h and Ω. Cover finite-jet coordinate changes, formal frame changes, ramified root changes with descent data, universal-object covers and compatible rank-one determinant transports. Construct the pullback comparison for a holomorphic map f:B′→B between smooth complex bases and prove that the resulting horizontal vector at (b′,m) is (v′,h_m(df(v′))). The corresponding algebraic stack pullback remains meaningful for general test bases, but analytic submersion statements require a smooth complex base.

Record the natural comparison isomorphisms for identity and composite base changes, the associativity pentagon, the identity triangles and compatibility with 2-isomorphic presentation arrows. On the rigidified phase spaces these descend to the required equalities/cocycle laws. Thus the construction is pseudofunctorial before rigidification and functorial up to the specified canonical comparisons afterward. Changes of determinant, weights, labels or formal local type that are not isomorphisms of the input remain genuine parameter changes or correspondences on stated domains. A time-dependent gauge matrix changes a formula but the compatible object and its transported tensors remain identified.
hypotheses: Isomorphisms of the same admitted decorated time problem and base maps preserving its specified data; the constructions of §§1.1–2.2.
Analytic output is over smooth complex bases; coarse-space comparisons use the scalar-gerbe descent from 1.3. Non-isomorphic parameter changes are not included among presentation arrows.

targets.name: meromorphicModuliToNonlinearConnection
targets.title: General construction theorem and reusable export
targets.statement:
Assemble §§1.1–2.3 into a construction from each admitted decorated time problem to its rigidified stable phase family and, over the open nonempty-fiber part of a smooth analytic time base, a holomorphic flat symplectic nonlinear connection (π:M→B,h,ω) in NonlinearConnections §§0.1 and 0.6, together with its closed total form Ω. The inputs contain curve and local connection data, a stability chamber and the determinant mode; they do not contain h, a scalar differential equation or a classification of surfaces. The result applies in arbitrary genus and admitted rank/polar degree for unfixed determinant; fixed-determinant export requires the separately proved comparison in §1.5 and the certified time transport in §1.2.

Give a single consumer certificate listing local-model admission, the actual time base, determinant verification, weight choice and nonemptiness evidence. Return the geometric carrier, the constructed tensors, dimension theorem at its exact scope, naturality and coherent pullback laws. A consumer proves only these admission conditions and its further specialized results. In particular neither relative dimension two nor one-dimensional time belongs to this construction theorem. Completeness, proper Riemann–Hilbert comparison, chosen observables, scalarization and distinguished solutions require their own downstream hypotheses and proofs. The construction theorem has the stated admission hypotheses and uses the named preceding construction and comparison theorems.
hypotheses: The admitted geometric input and time problem of 1.1–1.2; stable construction of 1.3–1.6 and the actual h, flatness and naturality from 2.1–2.3.
Restrict to the open nonempty-fiber time locus for a surjective nonlinear-connection carrier; a consumer must provide nonemptiness if its whole proposed base is claimed.
Fixed-determinant export additionally passes the independent determinant-fiber and rank-one transport gates.

targets.name: regularSingularRiemannHilbertSemiconjugacy
targets.title: Marked logarithmic Betti family and the full Riemann–Hilbert map
targets.statement:
For the logarithmic subproblem of §1.1, construct the topologically marked family of representation varieties of the punctured curves, their affine conjugacy quotients and the prescribed-local-character subfamilies. Keep the residue-exponent parameter λ on the de Rham side and the exponential characteristic-polynomial parameter a=rh(λ) on the Betti side. Repeat the bounded construction of §1.3 over the simultaneous residue parameter space Λ, and prove its comparison with the I13 family; the horizontal splitting is relative to fixed λ, so varying λ is not a time direction. On a marking cover the Betti family is identified by transport with a fixed character variety times the time base. This gives complete transport along all admissible time paths even when the character variety is singular; no smooth Betti tangent bundle is required.

Construct the holomorphic Riemann–Hilbert map from the entire stable logarithmic parabolic moduli of §1.3, including allowed reducible and resonant objects and all bundle types. Define it through the local system of horizontal sections and its conjugacy-quotient class, and prove descent from the universal-object cover. Identify this logarithmic moduli problem, its weights and residue ordering with the exact moduli functor used by I13; a matrix-chart comparison is insufficient. Prove that the actual strong splitting of §2.1 is semiconjugate to the marked Betti transport at every point, using the total integrable extension with its logarithmic lattices and the analytic dependence of local solutions. Prove local horizontal-lift existence independently of Riemann–Hilbert invertibility. At resonant or reducible points the map may have positive-dimensional fibers and is not replaced by an inverse map.

For a certified determinant transport, show that taking determinant of monodromy agrees with the rank-one Riemann–Hilbert map and that the prescribed determinant is a transported Betti section. Export the Hausdorff locally compact marked target and the full semiconjugacy as inputs to NonlinearConnections §0.4, without asserting properness until §2.6 or deducing source completeness here.
hypotheses: The logarithmic local subproblem of 1.1, the admitted pointed-curve time problem and fixed residue exponents of 1.2, and the actual stable moduli and strong connection of 2.4.
A topological marking cover of the punctured-curve family. Fixed-determinant conclusions require the verified determinant transport. The Betti target is allowed to be singular.

supporting_constructions.statement: Starting with CKG K4 on punctured curves, construct logarithmic extensions with chosen exponent lifts, parabolic flags and actual logarithmic lattices, prove the monodromy convention exp(−2πiλ), and prove the relevant regular-singular algebraic/analytic comparison. Include resonance, repeated residues and integer shifts of exponents with their lattice modifications; retain all bundle types. supporting_constructions.statement: Deligne II5.4 constructs the extension for a chosen section of ℂ→ℂ/ℤ; it explicitly does not make that canonical extension tensor-compatible. targets.name: regularSingularFamilyProperness
targets.title: Family properness in the exact logarithmic source scope
targets.statement:
For the full stable logarithmic parabolic moduli problem identified in §2.5, prove family properness of the marked Riemann–Hilbert map to the character family pulled back along the residue map rh:Λ_r^(n)(d)→A_r^(n). Use the complete exponent target (Rep_r(C,marked points)×_T T̃)×_{A_r^(n)}Λ_r^(n)(d), not only the generic smooth character locus. The exact source range is rank r≥2, n≥1, generic weights with stable=semistable, and rn−2r−2>0 when g=0, n>1 when g=1, n≥1 when g≥2. The residue space satisfies d+Σᵢⱼλⱼ^(i)=0. Prove the properness statement for families and its analytic base-change stability; properness of individual fibers alone is not the required result. The source theorem also supplies surjectivity and bimeromorphicity in this range, after the exact functor comparison.

For fixed determinant, construct the commutative determinant square on the de Rham and Betti moduli, prove the rank-one regular-singular Riemann–Hilbert isomorphism with the prescribed trace residues and logarithmic lattice, and identify the specified-determinant coarse moduli with the actual Cartesian inverse image of the corresponding determinant Betti section. Include the scalar-gerbe comparison: choosing a determinant identification must not silently change the coarse fiber. The section is transported only after the certificate of §1.2 and comparison of §2.5. Deduce fixed-determinant family properness by proper analytic base change along this proved square. This comparison is required even in genus zero; the simplification there must be proved.

Export the proper semiconjugacy certificate consisting of §§2.5–2.6. A consumer then invokes NonlinearConnections §0.4 with its own source and time domain to deduce complete horizontal continuation. Do not reprove that general continuation theorem here or extend this properness assertion to arbitrary irregular data.
hypotheses: The entire logarithmic moduli problem and Riemann–Hilbert map of 2.5, identified with I13; r≥2, n≥1 and fixed genus, degree and residue data with d+Σᵢⱼλⱼ^(i)=0.
Generic weights satisfying stable=semistable; g=0 requires rn−2r−2>0; g=1 requires n>1; g≥2 requires n≥1.
Fixed-determinant restriction additionally requires the proved Cartesian determinant comparison, rank-one regular-singular correspondence and certified transported determinant section.

targets.name: fivePointAdmittedInput
targets.title: Five logarithmic points with a nonempty stable input
targets.statement:
Take an ordered five-pointed genus-zero curve. After the unique normalization of the first three points to 0, 1, ∞, its time base is B = {(t₁,t₂) ∈ ℂ² : t₁,t₂ ∉ {0,1}, t₁ ≠ t₂}. Thus dim B = 2 is a conclusion of the marked-curve quotient; coordinates on B display that quotient. Take rank 2, structural divisor P = a₁+⋯+a₅, determinant (O,d) with its fixed identification and trivial strong time transport, and full logarithmic flags with ordered residue pairs (1/4,−1/4), (1/4,−1/4), (1/6,−1/6), (1/6,−1/6), (1/4,−1/4). Choose weights αᵢ,₁ = i/100 and αᵢ,₂ = i/100 + 2ⁱ⁻¹/1000 for i=1,…,5. All ten are distinct and 0<αᵢ,₁<αᵢ,₂<1. A rank-one stability wall would require 2deg F + Σᵢ εᵢ2ⁱ⁻¹/1000 = 0 with εᵢ=±1; the signed sum has odd numerator and absolute value ≤31/1000, so equality is impossible. Thus stable = semistable for these numerical data. These are inputs to MeromorphicConnectionModuli §§1.1–1.2; no classical degree-four condition is imposed.

Prove nonemptiness for every configuration, not by assuming a phase-space point. For generators with γ₁⋯γ₅ = 1 set D = diag(i,−i), J = [[0,1],[−1,0]], K = diag(exp(πi/3),exp(−πi/3)), and (M₁,…,M₅) = (D,J,K,K⁻¹,(DJ)⁻¹). Their product is I and all local spectra are distinct. D and J have no common invariant line, so the representation is irreducible. The regular-singular correspondence with chosen logarithms exp(−2πiλ), and local logarithmic lattice changes from the canonical extension when needed, produces a logarithmic connection with the specified residues and flags on each pointed curve. This statement concerns monodromy irreducibility, not constant-matrix residue eigenlines.

The trace residues vanish and determinant monodromy is trivial. The determinant logarithmic connection therefore extends without poles to a flat line connection on ℙ¹, isomorphic to (O,d); choose that identification. There is no invariant proper subbundle, hence stability for the chosen weights. As an additional check, any sum choosing one residue at each pole is [3(σ₁+σ₂+σ₅)+2(σ₃+σ₄)]/12 with σᵢ ∈ {−1,1}; its numerator is odd, so it is never an integer. This independently excludes a rank-one invariant subconnection by the residue/degree relation. Nonempty fibers on the whole B are proved; a global marked object on B is not assumed.
hypotheses: Ordered five distinct points on ℙ¹; specified rank, logarithmic residues, determinant identification and generic weights. The two-dimensional time quotient and nonempty stable fibers are outputs.

translation.title: 五つの対数極と空でない安定入力
translation.statement:
順序付き五点をもつ種数 0 の曲線をとる。最初の三点を 0、1、∞ に送る一意な正規化の後、時間基底は B = {(t₁,t₂) ∈ ℂ² : t₁,t₂ ∉ {0,1}, t₁ ≠ t₂} と表示される。したがって dim B = 2 は標識曲線の商から得る結論であり、B の座標はその商の表示である。階数 2、構造的因子 P = a₁+⋯+a₅、同定を指定した行列式 (O,d) とその自明な強い時間移送、順序付き留数対 (1/4,−1/4)、(1/4,−1/4)、(1/6,−1/6)、(1/6,−1/6)、(1/4,−1/4) をもつ完全対数的旗を用いる。i=1,…,5 に対して重み αᵢ,₁ = i/100、αᵢ,₂ = i/100 + 2ⁱ⁻¹/1000 を選ぶ。十個はすべて異なり、0<αᵢ,₁<αᵢ,₂<1 である。階数 1 の安定性の壁では 2deg F + Σᵢ εᵢ2ⁱ⁻¹/1000 = 0（εᵢ=±1）が必要になるが、符号和の分子は奇数で絶対値は 31/1000 以下なので成立しない。したがって、この数値データでは安定と半安定が一致する。これらを MeromorphicConnectionModuli §§1.1–1.2 の入力とする。古典的な次数 4 の条件を課さない。

相空間の点を仮定せず、すべての配置について非空性を証明する。γ₁⋯γ₅ = 1 を満たす生成元に対し、D = diag(i,−i)、J = [[0,1],[−1,0]]、K = diag(exp(πi/3),exp(−πi/3))、(M₁,…,M₅) = (D,J,K,K⁻¹,(DJ)⁻¹) とする。積は I であり、各局所スペクトルは相異なる。D と J に共通不変直線がないため、この表現は既約である。exp(−2πiλ) に対応する指定した対数と、必要なら標準拡張からの局所対数格子の変更を用いた確定特異対応により、各標識曲線上に指定した留数・旗をもつ対数接続が得られる。ここで用いるのはモノドロミーの既約性であり、留数行列に定数の共通固有直線がないという条件ではない。

トレース留数は零で、行列式モノドロミーは自明である。したがって行列式の対数接続は、ℙ¹ 上の極をもたない平坦線束接続へ延び、(O,d) と同型になる。その同定を選ぶ。不変な真部分束がないので、選んだ重みについて安定である。追加の確認として、各極で一つずつ留数を選んだ和は [3(σ₁+σ₂+σ₅)+2(σ₃+σ₄)]/12、σᵢ ∈ {−1,1} と書ける。分子は奇数なので整数にはならない。これも留数・次数関係によって階数 1 の不変部分接続を排除する。B 全体でファイバーが非空であることを証明し、B 上の大域的標識付き対象を仮定しない。
hypotheses: ℙ¹ 上の順序付き相異なる五点、指定した階数・対数留数・行列式の同定・一般の重みを用いる。時間の商の二次元性と安定ファイバーの非空性は出力である。
api: 標識曲線の実際の商を B と同定し、その固定された衝突判別集合を確認する。
既約モノドロミーの具体例、その指定対数による拡張、行列式の同定を構成する。
階数 2 の基礎束を自明と仮定せず、安定ファイバーの非空性を確認する。
tests: 積 D J K K⁻¹ (DJ)⁻¹ は厳密に I である。D の固有直線は座標軸であり、J はそれらを入れ替える。
留数差は 1/2 または 1/3 で非共鳴である。符号付き和の分子は奇数で、整数となる場合をすべて排除する。
五極を四極に置き換えると時間次元は 2 から 1 へ変わり、単なるチャート変更ではない。
留数行列に定数の共通固有直線がないことだけでは、微分加群の既約性の証拠にならない。

targets.name: fivePointConstructedDynamics
targets.title: Constructed flat symplectic dynamics in phase dimension four
targets.statement: Apply MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.4 to the verified input of §2.7. Its output is the full stable phase family π: M → B, retaining all allowed degree-zero bundle types, the relative trace symplectic form ω, and the constructed holomorphic flat splitting h. Verify the fixed-determinant comparison on genus zero. The general dimension formula gives 2·2²(0−1)+2+2(2−1)·5 = 4; fixing the determinant removes 2g = 0 directions here. Smoothness and symplecticity are construction outputs, not fields in the input. Use NonlinearConnections §0.6 for the closed total form, after the moduli construction has proved actual preservation of ω. The two commuting horizontal time directions exist intrinsically; no scalar Garnier formula or Hamiltonian coordinates are used.
hypotheses: The fully verified input and nonemptiness of 2.7; no phase space, splitting or symplectic form is supplied as input.

translation.title: 相空間四次元の平坦シンプレクティック力学系の構成
translation.statement: §2.7 で確認した入力に MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.4 を適用する。その出力は、許容される次数 0 の束の型をすべて保持した全安定相空間族 π: M → B、相対トレース・シンプレクティック形式 ω、および構成された正則平坦分裂 h である。種数 0 における行列式固定との比較を確認する。一般次元公式は 2·2²(0−1)+2+2(2−1)·5 = 4 を与え、この場合に行列式を固定して除かれる方向は 2g = 0 である。滑らかさとシンプレクティック性は構成の出力であり、入力の項目にしない。モジュライ構成が ω の実際の保存を証明した後で、NonlinearConnections §0.6 により閉じた全二形式を得る。可換な二つの水平時間方向は内在的に存在し、Garnier のスカラー公式や Hamilton 座標を用いない。
hypotheses: 2.7 の確認済み入力と非空性を用いる。相空間・分裂・シンプレクティック形式を入力として与えない。
api: 一般構成の許容条件と行列式比較を確認する。
同じ非線形接続対象、相対次元 4、閉じた全形式を提供する。
引戻しと表示の比較を同定し、時間次元 2 を保持する。
tests: ファイバー次元は −8+2+10=4 で、2 ではない。deg P=5 を古典的な予算に置き換えない。
平坦性だけでは e^{t₁}ω を保存しない。実際の保存定理を適用しなければならない。
大域的モジュライ族を、自明束上の行列チャートで置き換えない。

targets.name: fivePointProperRh
targets.title: A verified proper RH comparison
targets.statement:
Use MeromorphicConnectionModuli §§2.5–2.6, with I13 Theorem 2.2, on this logarithmic moduli problem. Verify g=0, r=2, n=5, rn−2r−2 = 4 > 0 and generic stability weights. Identify the constructed determinant-fixed moduli with the same determinant fiber of I13's family, using the rank-one determinant comparison and the actual coarse/gerbe comparison. Take the marked character family with the residue parameters retained through its fiber product with the exponent map λ ↦ exp(−2πiλ). Properness is a theorem about this actual family map, inherited through the proved Cartesian/base-change comparison. It is not a hypothesis in §2.7 or an inference from the existence of a foliation.

Use the complete Betti path transport of 2.5 and prove that the strong splitting of 2.8 maps every partial horizontal lift to that transport. Source and target comparisons use the full admitted moduli, rather than a chosen bundle chart. Only the regular-singular theorem is consumed. No general irregular properness or classical Painlevé continuation theorem is imported.
hypotheses: The actual logarithmic input and constructed connection of 2.7–2.8, with the checked I13 numerical range and the determinant/marking comparison. Properness and partial-lift compatibility are conclusions to verify via the general theorem.

api.name: fivePointProperRhLaw1
api.statement: Identify the precise I13 moduli and exponent-retaining Betti target after determinant fixing.

api.name: fivePointProperRhLaw2
api.statement: Verify properness by the proved Cartesian comparison and all-point horizontal compatibility.

tests.name: fivePointProperRhCheck1
tests.statement: Here 2·5−4−2=4>0; the source theorem is not applied without its genus/rank/pole inequality.

tests.name: fivePointProperRhCheck2
tests.statement: Forgetting the logarithms and retaining only their exponentials loses the properness statement.

tests.name: fivePointProperRhCheck3
tests.statement: Properness of RH does not say that π: M→B is proper.

translation.title: 確認された固有 RH 比較
translation.statement:
この対数モジュライ問題に、I13 Theorem 2.2 に基づく MeromorphicConnectionModuli §§2.5–2.6 を用いる。g=0、r=2、n=5、rn−2r−2 = 4 > 0、および一般の安定性重みを確認する。階数 1 の行列式比較と、実際の粗モジュライ・gerbe の比較を用いて、構成した行列式固定モジュライを I13 の族の同じ行列式ファイバーと同定する。指数パラメータの写像 λ ↦ exp(−2πiλ) とのファイバー積で留数パラメータを保持した、標識付き指標族を用いる。固有性は、この実際の族の写像についての定理であり、証明した Cartesian な基底変換比較から受け取る。§2.7 の仮定にはせず、葉層の存在からも推測しない。

同 §2.5 の完備な Betti 経路移送を用い、§2.8 の強い分裂がすべての部分水平持ち上げをこの移送へ送ることを証明する。源と標的の比較には許容された全モジュライを用い、選んだ束のチャートへ制限しない。ここで利用するのは確定特異な定理である。一般の不確定特異点の固有性や、古典的パンルヴェの延長定理は取り込まない。
hypotheses: 2.7–2.8 の実際の対数入力と構成された接続、確認した I13 の数値範囲、行列式・標識の比較を用いる。固有性と部分持ち上げとの両立性は、一般定理を通じて確認する結論である。
api: 行列式固定後の正確な I13 モジュライと、指数パラメータを保持する Betti 標的を同定する。
証明された Cartesian 比較による固有性と、全点での水平両立性を確認する。
tests: この場合は 2·5−4−2=4>0 である。種数・階数・極数の不等式を確認せず原典の定理を適用しない。
対数を忘れて指数値だけを保持すると、固有性の主張を失う。
RH の固有性は π: M→B の固有性を意味しない。

targets.name: fivePointCompleteTransport
targets.title: Reusing complete transport and its exact limits
targets.statement:
Apply NonlinearConnections §0.4 to §2.9 and obtain unique horizontal lifts through every point of every fiber for every compact piecewise C¹ path in B. Apply 0.3 for holomorphic local germs, 0.5 for the fundamental-groupoid action and the global horizontal section on a pointed universal cover of B, and 0.6 for symplectic preservation. The action and section are outputs of the constructed flat connection; descent to B holds exactly for fixed initial points of its nonlinear monodromy action.

When the proper RH family has been constructed on a topological marking cover, first lift the given path γ in B to that cover after choosing its initial marking. Apply the general proper-transfer theorem to the pulled-back connection and the lifted compact path, then project the resulting horizontal lift to M. The connection-preserving pullback map and local uniqueness prove independence of the initial marking and of overlapping marking charts. Thus completeness is asserted for all paths in B, without assuming a global topological marking of the five-punctured family.

This is the second actual consumer of the same general extension and descent proofs used for the classical family. Its transitive dependency closure excludes every Painlevé application target, including formal-profile enumeration, additive surface classification and scalar Painlevé formulas. This condition is checked on the expanded graph, not only on direct imports.

Do not apply the scalar first-jet theorem for a two-dimensional phase fiber to this four-dimensional fiber, or assert a one-variable pole statement on the two-dimensional base. For a connected holomorphic time curve f:C→B, choose c₀∈C and x₀∈M_(f(c₀)). Pull back the connection and construct its horizontal section on the pointed universal cover C̃ of C by 0.5. For an observer whose pullback along that section is defined and satisfies the non-infinity condition, apply 0.7 to obtain a meromorphic function on C̃. Prove that it descends to C exactly when its scalar evaluation is invariant under the actual deck action; this condition can be weaker than descent of the phase section. If a horizontal section on C is separately supplied, evaluate that section directly under the same observer hypotheses. Garnier coordinate dictionaries lie outside the four five-point application targets.
hypotheses: The constructed flat symplectic connection and verified proper semiconjugacy of 2.8–2.9. The curve-observer theorems additionally assume a connected holomorphic time curve, a base point, an initial phase point and the stated observer admissibility along the resulting universal-cover section. Descent to the curve additionally requires scalar deck invariance, or an independently supplied horizontal section on that curve.

api.name: fivePointCompleteTransportLaw1
api.statement: Instantiate the same completeness and groupoid-action theorems on a two-time/four-phase family.

api.name: fivePointCompleteTransportLaw2
api.statement: Verify no transitive dependency on the classical application.

api.name: fivePointCompleteTransportLaw3
api.statement: Prove the observer pullback theorem on the pointed universal cover of the time curve and the scalar-deck-invariance criterion for descent, under all the stated admissibility hypotheses.

tests.name: fivePointCompleteTransportCheck1
tests.statement: The expanded prerequisite graph excludes every Painlevé target, including its degree-four definition.

tests.name: fivePointCompleteTransportCheck2
tests.statement: Complete transport can have nontrivial monodromy; a universal-cover section need not descend.

tests.name: fivePointCompleteTransportCheck3
tests.statement: On a time curve the phase fiber still has dimension four, whereas a scalar first-jet fiber has dimension two; the scalar first-jet isomorphism cannot simply be asserted.

tests.name: fivePointCompleteTransportCheckCurveDescent
tests.statement: The generic flat complete connection q′=q/(2t) on ℂ××ℂ has horizontal germ q=√t through (1,1). The observer q is admissible, but its universal-cover value changes sign under one loop. Curve pullback and admissibility alone therefore do not imply scalar descent; 0.7 supplies the exact additional condition.

translation.title: 完備移送の再利用とその正確な範囲
translation.statement:
§2.9 に NonlinearConnections §0.4 を適用し、B 内の任意のコンパクトな区分的 C¹ 経路に対し、各ファイバーのすべての点を通る一意な水平持ち上げを得る。0.3 から正則な局所芽、0.5 から基本亜群の作用と基点付き普遍被覆上の大域水平切断、0.6 からシンプレクティック保存を得る。作用と切断は構成された平坦接続の出力であり、その非線形モノドロミー作用で初期点が固定される場合に、ちょうど B へ降下する。

固有 RH 族を位相的標識の被覆上で構成した場合、まず初期標識を選び、B 内の与えられた経路 γ をその被覆へ持ち上げる。引き戻した接続と持ち上げたコンパクト経路に一般の固有移送定理を適用し、得られた水平持ち上げを M へ射影する。接続を保つ引戻し写像と局所一意性により、初期標識と重なり合う標識チャートの選択から独立であることを証明する。これにより、五穿孔曲線族の大域的な位相標識を仮定せず、B 内のすべての経路について完備性を主張する。

これは、古典的族に使うものと同じ一般の延長・降下の証明の、実際の第二の利用例である。推移的な依存閉包はパンルヴェへの適用の全目標を除外し、形式プロファイルの列挙・加法型曲面分類・スカラーのパンルヴェ公式にも依存しない。直接の import だけでなく、展開したグラフでこの条件を検査する。

相ファイバー二次元の場合のスカラー第一ジェット定理を、この四次元ファイバーに適用しない。また、二次元基底上で一変数の極の主張をしない。連結な正則時間曲線f:C→B、基点c₀∈Cと初期点x₀∈M_(f(c₀))を選ぶ。接続を引き戻し、0.5からCの基点付き普遍被覆C̃上の水平切断を構成する。その切断に沿う引戻しが定義され、非恒等的無限大条件を満たす観測量に0.7を適用して、C̃上の有理型関数を得る。スカラー評価が実際の被覆変換作用に不変であることと、Cへ降下することの同値を証明する。この条件は相空間切断の降下条件より弱くなりうる。C上の水平切断が別途与えられている場合は、同じ観測量の仮定の下でその切断を直接評価する。Garnier 座標辞書は五極への適用の四目標の対象範囲に含めない。
hypotheses: 2.8–2.9 の構成済み平坦シンプレクティック接続と確認済み固有半共役を用いる。曲線上の観測量の定理では、連結な正則時間曲線・基点・初期点と、得られる普遍被覆上の切断に沿う観測量の許容性を追加で仮定する。曲線への降下にはスカラー評価の被覆変換不変性、または曲線上に別途与えた水平切断を要する。
api: 時間二次元・相空間四次元の族に、同じ完備性と亜群作用の定理を適用する。
古典的適用への推移的依存がないことを確認する。
時間曲線の基点付き普遍被覆上の観測量引戻しと、スカラー評価の被覆変換不変性による降下判定を、明記した全ての許容性仮定の下で証明する。
tests: 展開した前提グラフは、次数 4 の定義を含むすべてのパンルヴェ目標を除外する。
完備移送でもモノドロミーは非自明になりうる。普遍被覆上の切断が降下するとは限らない。
時間曲線に制限しても相ファイバーは四次元で、スカラー第一ジェットのファイバーは二次元である。スカラー第一ジェット同型をそのまま主張できない。

layers.title_ja: パンルヴェ方程式の内在的構成

targets.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoid
targets.title: Binding the general decorated-connection input
targets.statement: Use the objects and arrows of MeromorphicConnectionModuli §1.1 directly. This is an import binding, not a second definition of decorated connections. Record the determinant, local decorations, weights and marking that the classical restriction in §3.3 will retain. The genus-zero rank-two restriction is imposed there, not in the general framework. Identify the local presentations used in the Painlevé sources with these same objects, preserving filtrations, logarithmic lattices and ramified descent. The invariant adjoint and projective objects are End⁰(E) and the PGLᵣ connection; no globally trace-subtracted rank-r connection or square root of the determinant is introduced. (I23, §§2–4.)
hypotheses: An object of MeromorphicConnectionModuli 1.1, with its actual arrows, determinant and admitted local structures; no classical degree restriction yet.

locator.where: §2, Definitions 2.1–2.8; §§3–4

api.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Identify every imported object and arrow without copying its carrier.

api.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Verify the odd-determinant and resonant/ramified presentation comparisons on the classical inputs to be selected.

tests.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidCheck1
tests.statement: On E = O ⊕ O(−1), the determinant has odd degree; a putative global half-determinant twist does not exist. The carrier must still allow this bundle when the prescribed determinant matches it.

tests.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidCheck2
tests.statement: Two logarithmic residues with the same repeated eigenvalue, one scalar and one nonzero Jordan block, are not identified by specifying the eigenvalues. Their allowed parabolic objects and monodromy differ.

tests.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidCheck3
tests.statement: Changing the root w to −w in a rank-two ramified chart changes the displayed branches but gives an equivalent descended object; forgetting the descent arrow fails this check.

tests.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidCheck4
tests.statement: With I23's ramified convention, a rank-two ramified point contributes 2c + 1/2 to the residue/degree relation. Replacing it by 2c changes that relation by 1/2.

tests.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidCheck5
tests.statement: Rank zero is rejected before slope stability or the dimension formula is applied. At r = 1 the adjoint bundle End⁰(E) has rank zero, without changing the required positive rank of E.

tests.name: decoratedConnectionGroupoidCheck6
tests.statement: For A = 0 and frame change g = diag(z,1), g⁻¹dg = diag(1,0)dz/z; subtracting half its trace gives diag(1/2,−1/2)dz/z. The scalar discrepancy prevents gluing a rank-two trace-subtracted connection on E, while the induced End⁰(E) and PGL₂ connections glue.

hypotheses_ja: MeromorphicConnectionModuli 1.1 の対象、その実際の射、行列式、および許容局所構造を用いる。この段階では古典的な次数制限を課さない。

targets.name: reducedTimeDeformation
targets.title: Binding the general time-deformation problem
targets.statement: Use MeromorphicConnectionModuli §1.2 for the admitted deformation problem, its coordinate-change arrows, marking covers and fixed exponent parameters. For the classical subcategory verify the regular-singular determinant with fixed residues has the compatible time lift required by that contract. Identify the genus-zero local slices and their actual tangent maps; do not construct a second time-base carrier. The reduced versal problem remains the input to §3.3; its one-dimensionality is proved in §3.4. Strong isomonodromy preserves transported analytic data, not a fixed-coordinate irregular polynomial. (HEU10, Theorem 1.1; I23, §§5, 11.)
hypotheses: The imported decorated input and admitted deformation problem, with fixed exponent data; the classical determinant time-lift comparison must be verified.

locator.where: Theorem 1.1; Definitions 2.3/2.10; I23 §§5/11

api.name: reducedTimeDeformationApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Identify the fixed-parameter/time tangent decomposition through the imported construction.

api.name: reducedTimeDeformationApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Verify the determinant lift and genus-zero coordinate-change coherence required by the classical restriction.

tests.name: reducedTimeDeformationCheck1
tests.statement: Four ordered logarithmic points have one modulus after quotient by PGL₂: 4 − 3 = 1; its cross-ratio avoids 0, 1 and ∞.

tests.name: reducedTimeDeformationCheck2
tests.statement: A change τ = 2t multiplies the displayed horizontal generator by 1/2; retaining its coefficient unchanged gives a different parametrized system.

tests.name: reducedTimeDeformationCheck3
tests.statement: Two solutions with different movable pole sets use the same Bθ. A base that deletes one solution's poles fails this requirement.

hypotheses_ja: 取り込んだ付加構造付き入力と許容変形問題、および固定指数データを用いる。古典的行列式の時間方向への持ち上げとの比較は、この適用で確認する。

targets.name: classicalPainleveInput
targets.title: The rank-two degree-four subcategory
targets.statement:
Define the classical differential Painlevé input class by genus zero, rank two, a structural polar divisor of degree four, the local moduli conditions of §3.1, a regular-singular determinant connection with fixed residues and its compatible transport, the reduced versal formal-data deformation from §3.2, and nonempty stable fibers. On genus zero the determinant residues obey their sum = −degree convention for ∇ = d + A. The time deformation is the actual reduced deformation problem, not an arbitrarily chosen constant or nonversal curve in a larger base. Nonemptiness is a domain condition on the moduli problem; neither one-dimensional time nor continuation is a field of this definition. Prove the reduced-time dimension in §3.4, independently of the phase dimension. Keep the connection data themselves as objects; do not define this class as a six-element type. (VDPS09, §2.2 and Table 1; I23, Theorem 7.5.)

In the pole-budget comparison, r is the projective Katz invariant, computed from trace-free exponential differences. It is not the maximal slope of an arbitrary scalar twist of the connection. The classical determinant normalization avoids extra scalar irregular times. Adding an arbitrary scalar irregular part belongs to a separate rank-one extension with a specified strong time lift; it is not silently included in the one-dimensional deformation count. None of these local/formal comparisons requires a global square root of the determinant line.
hypotheses: Genus zero; rank two; structural degree four; regular-singular determinant with fixed compatible residues; reduced versal time problem; nonempty stable fibers.

locator.where: §2.2, Table 1; I23 Theorem 7.5 for downstream dimension

api.name: classicalPainleveInputLaw1
api.statement: Restrict the general connection functor to this full subcategory of input data and retain its arrows.

api.name: classicalPainleveInputLaw2
api.statement: Extract rank, genus and structural degree invariantly; prove their preservation under the stated equivalences.

api.name: classicalPainleveInputLaw3
api.statement: Compare the formal pole budget with Katz invariants: m = r + 1 for integral r, and m = r + 3/2 for a positive half-integral r in rank two.

api.name: classicalPainleveInputLaw4
api.statement: State nonemptiness and excluded discriminants explicitly on each parameter base, including exceptional logarithmic exponents.

tests.name: classicalPainleveInputCheck1
tests.statement: Four logarithmic points have budget 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4 and belong to this complexity class.

tests.name: classicalPainleveInputCheck2
tests.statement: Five logarithmic points have phase dimension 2·5 − 6 = 4, and three have phase dimension 2·3 − 6 = 0; neither is a two-dimensional Painlevé input.

tests.name: classicalPainleveInputCheck3
tests.statement: Two ramified points of Katz slope 1/2 have budget 2 + 2 = 4. Requiring integral slopes would lose this input.

tests.name: classicalPainleveInputCheck4
tests.statement: A logarithmic residue can vanish at a phase point without changing the structural degree. Recomputing the budget from its actual nonzero poles would wrongly remove that point.

hypotheses_ja: 種数0、階数2、構造的次数4、適合する留数を固定した確定特異な行列式接続、縮約されたversal時間変形問題、および非空な安定ファイバーを入力条件とする。

targets.name: classicalProfilesAndTimeDimension
targets.title: Classification of formal profiles and time normalizations
targets.statement:
Classify the allowed rank-two formal profiles of structural degree four, retaining the nondegenerate leading-term and reduced-deformation hypotheses. First classify underlying profiles after forgetting the order of the pole labels: enumerate partitions of four and the integral or half-integral generic local slope at each irregular part. This gives ten underlying profiles. Recover the original ordered input through its label-assignment groupoid: a permutation induces a reindexing equivalence between labelled presentations, not a label-preserving arrow in the original groupoid. There are seventeen ordered slope profiles, with counts 2, 8, 6 and 1 for one, two, three and four poles; the corresponding unordered counts are 2, 5, 2 and 1. These are counts of formal profile shapes, not of objects with continuous exponent parameters.

Prove that every labelled realization has one essential time parameter after quotienting the permitted label-preserving curve-coordinate changes. In a presentation with n poles the dimension calculation is n + Σ⌈rᵢ⌉ − 3 = Σmᵢ − 3 = 1, with the automorphism stabilizers and the chosen marking/slices explicitly checked. The determinant normalization and its transport remove no required projective direction and add no scalar irregular direction. Prove that all ten underlying presentations and every label assignment admit this determinant normalization. The table in §7.2 is a table of underlying profiles; its coordinate formulas are transported along the label-reindexing equivalences. (VDPS09, §2.2, Table 1, printed pp.18–19.)

Prove the familiar time domains only after fixing the displayed marking and normalization: the four-point cross-ratio base, a nonzero irregular time for the multiplicative-looking time charts, and an affine time for the polynomial charts. These are charts or marking covers of the intrinsic time problem; they are not six definitions of dynamics. The classification is restricted to this rank-two formal complexity, and does not classify every two-dimensional nonautonomous system.
hypotheses: An input of 3.3 with its allowed generic projective local types and the actual reduced formal-data deformation problem. Pole labels are retained. The number of profiles, automorphism-stabilizer calculation and one-dimensional reduced time are conclusions, not assumptions.

tests.name: classicalProfilesAndTimeDimensionCheck1
tests.statement: The ordered tuples (1,0,0) and (0,1,0) have orders (2,1,1) and (1,2,1). They have the same underlying profile but are not identified by a label-preserving arrow.

tests.name: classicalProfilesAndTimeDimensionCheck2
tests.statement: Enumerating ordered compositions of 4, with one local type for a part 1 and two for each larger part, gives 2 + 8 + 6 + 1 = 17. Forgetting order gives 2 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 10.

tests.name: classicalProfilesAndTimeDimensionCheck3
tests.statement: A label permutation preserves the pole budget and the time dimension, but transports the residue parameters and cross-ratio chart; it does not leave every displayed coordinate unchanged.

hypotheses_ja: §3.3の入力に、その許容された一般的位置の射影的局所型と、実際の縮約された形式データの変形問題を備える。極のラベルを保持する。プロファイルの個数、自己同型の固定部分群の計算、および縮約された時間の1次元性は、仮定ではなく結論である。

targets.name: stableConnectionModuli
targets.title: Classical specialization of the full stable moduli
targets.statement: Apply MeromorphicConnectionModuli §1.3 to §3.3. Verify its determinant, stability and local-model admission hypotheses on the classical input; boundedness is supplied by the general construction. Identify its output with the full classical stable moduli problem. The stack, rigidification, coarse family and étale universal-object covers are the imported constructions. Retain all permitted bundle types and the actual residual μ₂ stabilizer before rigidification. Own the comparison of every classical framed chart with its actual locally closed or open locus; a balanced chart never replaces the entire moduli space. (I23, Theorem 5.1.)
hypotheses: The classical input 3.3; verify the exact hypotheses of the general stable-moduli construction rather than assuming its representing family.

locator.where: Theorem 5.1 and §10 setup

api.name: stableConnectionModuliApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Identify the classical moduli functor with the restricted general functor, including arrows and determinant identification.

api.name: stableConnectionModuliApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Verify every framed chart inclusion, its complement, and the weight-chamber common stable loci.

tests.name: stableConnectionModuliCheck1
tests.statement: A stable object may have scalar automorphisms before rigidification. A set-valued quotient that claims all stabilizers were trivial fails this example.

tests.name: stableConnectionModuliCheck2
tests.statement: A family can leave a trivial-bundle chart by bundle jumping while remaining in the moduli space. Its phase path is not declared singular for that reason.

tests.name: stableConnectionModuliCheck3
tests.statement: In the extension family 0 → O(−1) → E_t → O(1) → 0, E₀ = O(−1) ⊕ O(1) while E_t = O ⊕ O for t ≠ 0. The two splitting strata pull back to {0} and its complement in A¹; the first is not open. The full connection moduli must retain such bundle jumps on the permitted connection locus.

tests.name: stableConnectionModuliCheck4
tests.statement: A ramified generic local factor is irreducible, so it has no global ∇-invariant line and is stable for every weight; this is I23 Remark 2.9, not a claim that every special solution is absent.

hypotheses_ja: 古典的入力 3.3 を用いる。表現する族を仮定せず、一般の安定モジュライ構成の正確な仮定を確認する。

targets.name: connectionDeformationComplex
targets.title: Specializing the deformation complex and pairing
targets.statement: Specialize MeromorphicConnectionModuli §1.4 to the determinant-fixed family of §3.5, and prove that infinitesimal classical families and gauges correspond to its cocycles and coboundaries. Use its actual three-term ramified cone and ℂ-linear differential-operator/Čech construction. Do not replace the commutator differential by an O-linear map, or truncate the cone without a proved quasi-isomorphism. Verify the determinant restriction and trace-sign convention on the same complex. (I23, equation (6.9), Propositions 6.3 and 7.2.)
hypotheses: The family of 3.5 and its determinant and local structures; the tangent/obstruction identifications are imported via the verified comparison.

locator.where: §6 (6.9), Proposition 6.3; §7 Proposition 7.2

api.name: connectionDeformationComplexApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Construct the restriction comparison with the general cone, including the determinant-fixed tangent directions.

api.name: connectionDeformationComplexApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Verify gauge, trace-sign and local-presentation compatibility under this comparison.

tests.name: connectionDeformationComplexCheck1
tests.statement: An infinitesimal gauge change by u changes a connection representative by the commutator differential of u; its tangent class is zero.

tests.name: connectionDeformationComplexCheck2
tests.statement: Without a determinant identification scalars have an infinitesimal automorphism direction; fixing it in characteristic zero removes that direction, although the finite μ₂ stabilizer remains until rigidification.

tests.name: connectionDeformationComplexCheck3
tests.statement: With ω = dq ∧ dp, the ordered tangent pair (∂q, ∂p) has pairing +1 and the reversed pair −1; a reversed trace convention must be corrected before transport formulas are used.

hypotheses_ja: 3.5 の族、行列式、および局所構造を用いる。接空間・障害との同定は、確認した比較を通じて一般構成から得る。

targets.name: relativeSymplecticModuli
targets.title: The classical symplectic surface as a construction output
targets.statement: Apply MeromorphicConnectionModuli §§1.5–1.6 to the family and complex identified in §§3.5–3.6. Verify the determinant-fiber comparison; genus zero contributes no omitted Jacobian directions. Substituting g = 0, r = 2 and deg P = 4 in the admitted general dimension theorem gives 2. Smoothness, nondegeneracy and relative closedness are outputs. The finite-flat auxiliary unfolding, its simple-connection moduli, both generic logarithmic quasi-isomorphisms and the smooth-density argument are proved once in the general framework, before any confluence theorem. Here identify its central stable fiber, complex and form with the actual classical family, including admissible nonreduced base change. Do not invoke targets 9.5–9.8. (I23, Theorems 7.5 and 8.1, Propositions 8.2–8.3.)
hypotheses: The classical family and its comparison with the general deformation construction; smoothness, dimension two and the symplectic form are conclusions.

locator.where: Theorems 7.5/8.1; Propositions 8.2–8.3 and (8.2)

api.name: relativeSymplecticModuliApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Verify the fixed-determinant and central-fiber comparisons needed to specialize the general theorem.

api.name: relativeSymplecticModuliApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Export the same relative tangent bundle and symplectic form on the entire classical family.

tests.name: relativeSymplecticModuliCheck1
tests.statement: Genus zero, rank two and degree four give −8 + 2 + 8 = 2; structural degree five instead gives 4.

tests.name: relativeSymplecticModuliCheck2
tests.statement: Fixing the determinant in positive genus removes 2g directions when the determinant-map comparison applies; the genus-zero coincidence cannot be exported unchanged.

tests.name: relativeSymplecticModuliCheck3
tests.statement: A skew pairing which vanishes identically is closed but is not symplectic; nondegeneracy must follow from the actual duality computation.

tests.name: relativeSymplecticModuliCheck4
tests.statement: At r = 1 and g = 1 the unfixed-determinant formula gives 2, and fixing the entire line connection gives 0. The rank-zero input that would incorrectly give 2 is outside the domain.

tests.name: relativeSymplecticModuliCheck5
tests.statement: For r = 2, local order 2 and q₁ = 2, the unfolding equation is (z − 2h²)(z − h²). Its fiber at h = 0 is z² and at h = 1 is (z − 2)(z − 1); modulo h² it is again z². Check the central and pulled-back complexes and forms, rather than identifying this family with fixed distinct sections.

hypotheses_ja: 古典的族と一般変形構成との比較を用いる。滑らかさ、二次元性、シンプレクティック形式は結論である。

targets.name: exceptionalStrataRetained
targets.title: Exceptional strata are part of the phase space
targets.statement: Prove that the construction retains all w-stable logarithmic resonance, reducible and apparent-singularity strata allowed by its fixed local moduli conditions. Describe how the local filtration resolves the ambiguity of repeated eigenvalues. Record nonemptiness separately. At generic ramified points use the irreducibility theorem rather than inventing reducible objects there. Targets 4.1–4.4 will identify the images of these already constructed strata in the character space. A vanishing leading irregular coefficient changes the input stratum and is handled by §7.3 and targets 9.5–9.8. (I23, §2 and Remark 2.9; IIS06, §4, especially Theorems 4.10–4.12; VDPS09, §2.2 and §3.)
hypotheses: All stable resonant, reducible and apparent strata allowed by the fixed local conditions; generic ramified local irreducibility.
hypotheses_ja: 固定した局所条件で許容される、安定な共鳴・可約・見かけの特異点の各層をすべて含め、一般的位置の分岐局所モデルの既約性を用いる。

targets.name: strongIsomonodromySplitting
targets.title: Specializing the strong isomonodromy construction
targets.statement: Apply MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.1 to the classical time problem and the family of targets 3.5–3.8. Identify its strong extensions with the classical universal-object charts, including kernel lattices, logarithmic flags and ramified descent. The total pole class is Ω¹_X(log D) ⊗ O_X(P − D); its moving-coordinate generators dz/zᵐ and dε/zᵐ⁻¹ remain comparison lemmas, with a regular time coefficient at a logarithmic pole. Import existence, uniqueness and gluing of strong extensions, and obtain the same splitting h of NonlinearConnections §0.1. This target does not assume h or recover it from a prescribed scalar equation. (I23, Definition 10.1, Propositions 10.7 and 10.10.)
hypotheses: The constructed classical moduli/time problem; verify that its local structures and determinant transport satisfy the strong-extension contract.

locator.where: Definition 10.1, (10.1), Propositions 10.7/10.10, (11.2)

api.name: strongIsomonodromySplittingApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Compare the classical kernel lattices and moving-pole filtration with the general strong-extension class.

api.name: strongIsomonodromySplittingApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Identify the resulting tangent splitting, its linearity and its base-change maps without creating a second connection object.

tests.name: strongIsomonodromySplittingCheck1
tests.statement: A zero time tangent lifts to zero; adding an arbitrary vertical vector would violate uniqueness of the integrable extension.

tests.name: strongIsomonodromySplittingCheck2
tests.statement: Rescaling the time tangent by 2 rescales its lift by 2, while changing the time coordinate to 2t rescales the normalized generator by 1/2.

tests.name: strongIsomonodromySplittingCheck3
tests.statement: The zero map cannot be a splitting over a nonzero time tangent because dπ ∘ 0 = 0 ≠ id.

hypotheses_ja: 構成済みの古典的モジュライ・時間問題を用いる。その局所構造と行列式の移送が、強い拡張の契約を満たすことを確認する。

targets.name: isomonodromySplittingFlat
targets.title: The imported flatness theorem on classical inputs
targets.statement: Use MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.2 and the identification of §3.9 to obtain h([v,w]) = [h(v),h(w)] on the classical family. Verify that the two-parameter strong-extension comparison restricts to this time problem. The general mixed-term proof is not repeated for each formal profile; no analytic Stokes theorem or scalar equation is a premise. (I23, Theorem 11.6.)
hypotheses: The strong splitting identified in 3.9 and the verified restriction of the general two-parameter extension problem.

locator.where: Theorem 11.6 and mixed second-order extension proof

api.name: isomonodromySplittingFlatApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Verify the restriction comparison for the mixed extension and export the bracket identity.

hypotheses_ja: 3.9 で同定した強い分裂と、一般の二パラメータ拡張問題の制限比較を用いる。

targets.name: closedTotalSymplecticForm
targets.title: Symplectic preservation and total form by general comparison
targets.statement: First specialize the actual symplectic-preservation theorem of MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.2. Flatness by itself does not supply preservation. Then apply NonlinearConnections §0.6 to (π,h,ω) and obtain the closed total form Ω(v,w) = ω(v − h(dπv), w − h(dπw)), its kernel and transport laws. Identify this form with the classical family, rather than introducing a second Hamiltonian object. A Darboux/time chart and local exactness give the downstream expression dq ∧ dp + dH ∧ dt. (I23, Definition 11.4 and Corollary 11.8.)
hypotheses: The constructed relative form and splitting, plus the verified specialization of the moduli symplectic-preservation theorem; preservation is not inferred from flatness.

locator.where: Definition 11.4, Corollary 11.8; BOA01 Theorems 7.1/7.3 at their scope

api.name: closedTotalSymplecticFormApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Identify the imported relative and total forms and their horizontal kernel.

api.name: closedTotalSymplecticFormApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Verify Hamiltonian signs and time-dependent coordinate comparisons only after choosing the stated local charts.

tests.name: closedTotalSymplecticFormCheck1
tests.statement: For H = p²/2, contraction with ∂t + p∂q annihilates dq ∧ dp + p dp ∧ dt; using the opposite sign does not.

tests.name: closedTotalSymplecticFormCheck2
tests.statement: H and H + t² give the same vertical vector field and extended two-form, but different scalar functions.

tests.name: closedTotalSymplecticFormCheck3
tests.statement: On a symplectic fiber, Ω has no nonzero vertical kernel vector; degenerating ω to zero would fail this characterization.

hypotheses_ja: 構成した相対形式と分裂、およびモジュライのシンプレクティック保存定理の特殊化を用いる。平坦性から保存を推測しない。

targets.name: presentationNaturality
targets.title: Coherent restriction of the general construction
targets.statement: Use MeromorphicConnectionModuli §§2.3–2.4 to identify all objects in targets 3.1–3.12 as the classical restriction of one construction, with coherent presentation, gauge and admissible base-change comparisons. Verify the cocycle diagrams for the classical markings and time slices. Changes of labels, determinant or stability chamber remain the explicitly permitted morphisms or correspondences, with stated domains. A later coordinate dictionary must commute with this construction; it is not a new definition of the dynamics.
hypotheses: The verified classical restrictions of the general construction and their actual presentation-change arrows.

locator.where: Theorem 1.1; I23 Propositions 10.7/10.10

api.name: presentationNaturalityApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Prove the classical specialization square and its triple-overlap coherence.

api.name: presentationNaturalityApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Keep all imported structures on one moduli family and one nonlinear connection.

hypotheses_ja: 一般構成の古典的制限として確認された対象と、実際の表示変更の射を用いる。

layers.title: Riemann–Hilbert comparison and the Painlevé property
layers.title_ja: Riemann–Hilbert 比較とパンルヴェ性

targets.name: sectorialStokesDescent
targets.title: Sectorial local systems and ramified analytic descent
targets.statement: Construct the analytic classification of the permitted local meromorphic connections by formal graded data, sectorial solutions and Stokes transition maps, retaining resonant logarithmic lattices and flags. Prove sectorial existence, overlap uniqueness, cocycle identities and analytic dependence on the admissible time parameters. At a ramified point perform the construction on the finite cover and prove equivariant descent, including the deck permutation of the exponential factors. A formal Laurent-series classification alone does not prove these analytic assertions. (I23, §9, Theorem 9.7 and Corollary 9.11; BOA01, §§3–6; HEU10, §2; BY15, Remark 3 and Definitions 7 and 13.)
hypotheses: Admitted good rank-two formal types; resonant logarithmic lattice data; finite ramified covering and deck action.

locator.where: §9 Theorem 9.7/Corollary 9.11; BOA01 §§3–6; BY15 Definitions 7/13

api.name: sectorialStokesDescentLaw1
api.statement: Construct solution-sector restriction, refinement and change of sectorial normalization.

api.name: sectorialStokesDescentLaw2
api.statement: Recover the actual local analytic connection and prove full faithfulness on decorated objects.

api.name: sectorialStokesDescentLaw3
api.statement: Compare the logarithmic, unramified and ramified descriptions through the same descent language.

api.name: sectorialStokesDescentLaw4
api.statement: Prove that integrable time extension is equivalent to strong local constancy of these data at the stated local scope.

tests.name: sectorialStokesDescentCheck1
tests.statement: A rank-one exponential exp(1/z) has irregular growth despite trivial ordinary monodromy; ordinary monodromy alone cannot classify the object.

tests.name: sectorialStokesDescentCheck2
tests.statement: A nontrivial unipotent logarithmic monodromy matrix differs from the identity although both eigenvalues equal 1.

tests.name: sectorialStokesDescentCheck3
tests.statement: On a quadratic cover, one full turn in z exchanges the two formal exponential branches; a sectorial construction that returns each branch individually without the deck action fails descent.

targets.name: completeBettiTransport
targets.title: The Betti family and complete transport
targets.statement:
For the regular-singular subcategory, use MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.5 and verify that its marked Betti family agrees with this target. The genuinely irregular and ramified transport extensions remain the scoped obligations below.

Construct the generalized monodromy groupoid by gluing the local data of §4.1 with the global local system on the punctured curve. Keep the enriched groupoid with logarithmic lattices and flags distinct from the ordinary affine character quotient obtained by forgetting those decorations. In the ordinary quotient impose the closed spectral-invariant and determinant constraints, and retain the exponent parameter θ as a separate fiber-product coordinate. At resonance do not fix a single nonclosed Jordan conjugacy class: scalar and allowed unipotent strata with the prescribed spectrum must remain present. Construct locally constant transport along admissible marked deformations, including changes of Stokes-sector presentations. Prove composition and inverse laws and completeness along every compact path in Bθ. A singular character fiber is permitted; transport is defined by the groupoid/topological construction, not by an assumed smooth tangent splitting there. (VDPS09, §§1–3; BOA14, §10, Theorem 10.2; BY15, Proposition 19, Theorem 21 and Corollary 22.)

BOA14's cited family-transport theorem has untwisted scope. Extend its isotopy construction to the rank-two ramified objects of BY15 by retaining the exponential covering, grading and deck action, constructing deck-compatible equivalences of the Stokes groupoids, and descending the framing action and closed spectral constraints. Prove independence, composition and homotopy compatibility before concatenating local products along a compact path. BY15's quasi-Hamiltonian/Poisson theorem by itself is not this family-transport theorem.
hypotheses: The local analytic data of 4.1 over the admitted marked time problem of 3.2, retained exponent lifts, and fixed closed spectral/determinant constraints; singular affine quotients are permitted. Ramified family isotopy, descent and complete transport are outputs.

locator.where: §10 Theorem 10.2; BY15 Proposition 19/Theorem 21/Corollary 22

api.name: completeBettiTransportApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Construct restriction, gluing, gauge-conjugation and change-of-marking functors.

api.name: completeBettiTransportApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Distinguish the decorated groupoid, its categorical quotient and the locus where it represents individual orbits.

api.name: completeBettiTransportApplicationLaw3
api.statement: Prove local product descriptions over simply connected admissible time neighborhoods and their continuation along finite chains.

api.name: completeBettiTransportApplicationLaw4
api.statement: Define the complete transport on the coarse quotient and its lift on any required decoration space.

tests.name: completeBettiTransportCheck1
tests.statement: θ and θ + 1 give the same exponential eigenvalue but need not give the same logarithmic lattice; the comparison target retains θ.

tests.name: completeBettiTransportCheck2
tests.statement: A reducible representation and its semisimplification can have the same coarse character. The quotient is not declared a faithful encoding of all connection objects.

tests.name: completeBettiTransportCheck3
tests.statement: Transport around a nontrivial loop may act nontrivially on the fiber; completeness does not imply trivial monodromy.

supporting_constructions.statement: 2.5 constructs the finite-type representation varieties and their reductive affine conjugacy quotients using the proven 1.3 invariant-theory prefix, then applies 1.2 analytification and proves Hausdorff/local-compactness and marked product transport, including singular points. 4.2 constructs the wild/Stokes framing groupoid and quotient at its actual reductive or explicitly descended stages; unipotent local Stokes groups do not by themselves permit an arbitrary GIT quotient. Prove root/deck isotopy and ramified descent, stabilizer compatibility and all-stratum holomorphic maps. Nothing in SSF1.17 supplies these constructions automatically.
supporting_constructions.statement_ja: 2.5 は 1.3 の不変式論を用いて有限型表現多様体と簡約群によるアフィン共役商を構成し、1.2 の解析化を適用して特異点を含む Hausdorff 性・局所コンパクト性・標識付き積移送を証明する。4.2 は wild/Stokes のフレーム亜群と、実際に簡約群商または降下が正当化される各段階の商を構成する。局所 Stokes 群が冪単であることから任意の GIT 商を推論しない。根・被覆変換を保つ isotopy、分岐降下、安定化群との両立、全層での正則写像を証明する。SSF1.17 をこれらの構成の代用にしない。

targets.name: fullPhaseRiemannHilbert
targets.title: Riemann–Hilbert and compatibility on the whole phase space
targets.statement:
The regular-singular RH map and its all-point horizontal compatibility are imported through MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.5, after identifying the same parabolic moduli and residue-parameter target. This import does not discharge the irregular local reconstruction.

Construct RHθ: Mθᵃⁿ → Rθ over Bθ by the analytic classification and prove that it is holomorphic. Prove that it sends every horizontal trajectory of §3.9 to the transport of §4.2, including trajectories inside resonance, reducible and exceptional loci. On the stated stable irreducible/nonresonant open locus prove the inverse comparison; elsewhere record the actual fibers and decoration data rather than asserting injectivity. Compare the integrable-extension construction with the local analytic reconstruction, and descend from universal-object covers. (IIS06, Theorems 4.10–4.12; IS12, Theorem 5.1; I23, §9 and §11.)

The theorem's all-strata scope is a construction target: the generic unramified theorem is one of its inputs, not a replacement for the missing resonant or ramified comparison. No scalar equation is used in the extension across these loci.
hypotheses: The full stable moduli family of 3.5/3.8, the strong splitting of targets 3.9–3.12, and the decorated analytic reconstruction and Betti family of 4.1–4.2. Holomorphic descent and all-source horizontal compatibility are to be proved; an inverse is asserted only on the specified irreducible/nonresonant locus.

locator.where: Theorems 4.10–4.12; IS12 Theorem 5.1; I23 §§9/11

api.name: fullPhaseRiemannHilbertApplicationLaw1
api.statement: Construct the holomorphic RH map from the universal-object cover and prove descent and base-change naturality.

api.name: fullPhaseRiemannHilbertApplicationLaw2
api.statement: Compare the decorated local reconstruction with the forgetful ordinary character quotient.

api.name: fullPhaseRiemannHilbertApplicationLaw3
api.statement: Prove horizontal compatibility at every retained point and the inverse theorem only on its stated open locus.

tests.name: fullPhaseRiemannHilbertCheck1
tests.statement: Two distinct points on an exceptional fiber can have the same ordinary character; the construction must not choose one as an inverse.

tests.name: fullPhaseRiemannHilbertCheck2
tests.statement: At a resonant logarithmic point, equal eigenvalues do not justify deleting either the allowed scalar or unipotent stratum.

tests.name: fullPhaseRiemannHilbertCheck3
tests.statement: Retaining exponent lifts distinguishes θ from θ + 1 even when their ordinary exponential eigenvalues agree.

additional_source_refs: I13: Theorem 2.2 and regular-singular family comparison
hypotheses_ja: §3.5・§3.8の安定モジュライ族全体、目標3.9–3.12の強い分裂、および§§4.1–4.2の付加構造付き解析的再構成とBetti族を入力とする。正則降下と、始域全体での水平性の適合は証明すべき事項である。逆写像は、指定した既約・非共鳴部分でのみ主張する。

targets.name: properClassicalRiemannHilbert
targets.title: Proper comparison for the full classical input class
targets.statement:
On the four-logarithmic-point branch, verify 2·4 − 2·2 − 2 = 2 > 0 and the fixed-determinant/marking comparison, then apply MeromorphicConnectionModuli §2.6 (I13, Theorem 2.2). The source retains the exponent parameters by a fiber product. No general irregular properness is inferred from this regular-singular theorem; the all-classical extension below remains an owned target.

For each admitted degree-four rank-two input and every allowed exponent parameter, prove that RHθ is proper as a map of the whole time family, with the exponent lift retained in its target, on the full stable moduli space of §3.5. Establish the corresponding family statement on admitted parameter charts; properness of each fixed-time map is not sufficient. The target has the ordinary generalized character data with its fixed closed constraints; no solution-dependent open subset is removed. State surjectivity onto the realizable component separately from properness. This includes resonant logarithmic and stable reducible points and the generic ramified local structures defining the classical class. (IIS06, Definition 2.11 and Theorems 4.10–4.12; IS12, Theorem 5.1 and the scope warning of Remark 6.3; HEU10, Theorem 1.1.)

The required extension is owned here. Develop the proof through four concrete intermediate results: boundedness of local lattices uniformly over compact families of generalized characters with fixed exponent lifts; extension of the retained flags and factorized structures in a relative projective parameter space with their closed incidence relations; semistable replacement after the necessary base change and elementary modifications, followed by semistable = stable for the chosen weights and uniqueness in the separated moduli problem; and compatibility of these extensions with global gluing and the analytic moduli topology. Stability is open but is not thereby preserved by arbitrary limits. Verify that these results give compact inverse images of compact subsets, rather than merely closed fibers or pointwise solvability. A projective flag variety alone does not prove the theorem, since the underlying connection may also escape.

HEU10's universal strong isomonodromic deformation gives an independent possible route to the continuation conclusion of §4.6. Such a route must establish the identification of the time bases, extension of local decorations, determinant and stability preservation, bundle-jumping compatibility, descent, and equality with §3.9. It does not by itself prove the properness required in this target. I23's global foliation theorem and IS12's generic theorem also do not discharge it. The compactness theorem remains an explicit internal proof-development task.
hypotheses: The RH map constructed in 4.3 for the full admitted classical time/parameter family, with exponent lifts and closed character constraints retained, and every allowed stable source stratum. Uniform lattice bounds, extension of decorations, stable replacement, compact containment and relative properness are not assumed; this target owns their proofs.

locator.where: Definition 2.11/Theorems 4.10–4.12; IS12 Theorem 5.1/Remark 6.3; full-classical extension is an owned proof target
